text:
Cardiology clinic - six month review

62M, ex-smoker (stopped 2011), seen six months after CABG x3.

Symptoms
NYHA II on inclines only. No rest angina, no orthopnoea, no PND. Walking the dog twice a day
without stopping.

O/E
Sternotomy well healed. JVP not raised. HS I + II + 0. Chest clear, no peripheral oedema.
BP 138/84 sitting, HR 62 and regular.

Bloods
Creatinine today 1.7 mg/dL, up from 1.2 in January. K 4.6, Hb 12.1. Repeat U&E in two weeks
before we touch the ramipril.

Background
Three-vessel disease at angiography, grafted electively on 6 November 2024. No history of
myocardial infarction. Father had an MI in his fifties and a second one at 61, which killed him.

Impression: stable revascularised ischaemic heart disease with a creeping creatinine, most
likely ACE related.

Plan: repeat bloods 2/52, hold the ramipril dose, review in six months. If the creatinine has
not settled we would consider stopping the ACE inhibitor altogether.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Admitted 17/05/2026. Discharged 19/05/2026. Ward B4, under Dr Okonjo.

Presenting complaint
Central chest tightness at rest, 40 minutes, settled with GTN in the ambulance.

Inpatient course
Serial troponin flat at 14 then 15 ng/L. ECG unchanged from the 2024 tracing. Myocardial
infarction was excluded on this admission. He was pain free from arrival and mobilised on the
ward without symptoms.

Chest wall tenderness was reproducible on palpation over the left costal margin, and the pain is
more likely musculoskeletal than cardiac.

CT head, requested by the medical registrar after a witnessed collapse in the department,
reported an old right occipital infarct unchanged since 2019. He had not been told about this
before and it was discussed with him at length prior to discharge.

Query paroxysmal AF as the cause of the collapse. A 7 day holter has been fitted and the result
will go to the cardiology clinic.

Discharge medication unchanged: bisoprolol 5 mg od, atorvastatin 80 mg nocte, aspirin 75 mg od,
ramipril 5 mg od.

Telephone triage 08:40.

Rash both shins x3 days. No fever, no blistering, not systemically unwell. No new medication and
no new soap or washing powder.

Says the chest has been fine since the May admission, no further tightness, taking all four
tablets.

Asked directly: no bleeding, no black stools, no bruising on the aspirin.

Booked face to face with the duty GP tomorrow am for the rash. Safety netted for fever or
spreading redness.
